links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: We should use the approval module that comes with the ERP we already have.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Wait, the bundled one? I thought that was extra.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: It's priced, yeah, eleven thousand a year. But hold on, that's the part-

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Eleven thousand is not nothing.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: It's not, but let me finish. We're already licensed for the platform, so there's no new vendor, no new contract, nothing to onboard.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: And configuring it is about two weeks, they said. Two weeks of setup. There's no data migration, because the vendors and the GL codes are already sitting in there.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: Two weeks, that sounds, I mean, that sounds optimistic. When we did the expense thing it was, what, six?

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: That was a different thing, that moved data from three places. This doesn't move anything.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Okay but what do we actually get out of it? Like, in numbers.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Right, so I pulled the timestamps from last quarter. Median time from invoice received to approved is nine days right now. With routing in the module it should land around three.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Nine days? Median? Not the average?

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Median. The average is worse, there's a long tail of stuff stuck over a month.

links.speaker: Ivan
links.quote: Is that, um, nine days including the ones that go to the regional offices?

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Yes, all of it.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: It's a lot. I think maybe, um, it also affects the early-pay discounts, doesn't it?

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: It does, we've been missing a couple of those.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Okay. Back to- can I push on the price a bit?

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Go ahead, that's fair.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Eleven thousand a year, every year. If we get a better tool in six months we're, we're stuck paying that?

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: It's annual. We could stop renewing. And what's the alternative, nothing? Because right now the cost is people chasing approvals by hand.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: I'm not saying nothing. I'm saying, did anyone look-

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Um, Ravi, I think nobody has brought another one to me. Has someone?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: No. Not yet. I just don't love picking the first thing we see.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: It's also the one with the least risk, though. Honestly I'd argue it's the boring choice and that's why it works.

links.speaker: Ivan
links.quote: Um, so the, the approval limits. Who sets those? Because right now it's kind of, it lives in Stefan's head.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: They'd be set up in the config. Tiers by amount, and by cost center. We'd need to write them down first, which we should do anyway.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: Oh, that reminds me, the audit people wanted the thresholds written down too. Last year they asked and we sort of, we showed them an email from, from like twenty-nineteen.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Not great.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: Not great, no.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: So that, that's another reason, I think. Um.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Right. It gives us a paper trail without extra work.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Fine, but two weeks of whose time? Because month-end is coming.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Mostly mine and the ERP admin's. Maybe a few hours from Pavel for the vendor master cleanup.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: A few hours I can do. If it's, you know, not the week of the close.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Yeah, okay. Um. Does anyone, does anybody have a real objection? Like something that would stop us?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Not a stop. I'd want the renewal date in writing, so we know when we can walk.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: I'll ask for it. I'll put it in the order form request.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Then I'm okay.

links.speaker: Ivan
links.quote: I'm okay with it too. I mean, yes.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Okay. Good. Pavel, could you get the configuration work on the calendar, with the ERP admin, for maybe the first week after the close? Um, sorry, I mean, something like that.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: Sure. I'll check what Sanne's free, uh, I mean the admin's free, and send invites tomorrow.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Send me the draft so I can block the days.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: Will do.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Thank you. Um, and I'll tell Emeka we have a plan, he'll be glad.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Tell him the nine days number. He likes numbers.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: I will. Okay, other things. Did anybody hear about the team lunch?

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: Is that the Thursday one? Because I have the thing with, uh, the- no, sorry, I have a thing Thursday.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Maybe Friday then. Ivan, does Friday work?

links.speaker: Ivan
links.quote: Friday's fine.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Friday's good for me, I'm in anyway.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: I can do Friday if it's before one. I've got a call.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Okay, I think maybe noon. I'll ask the place if they have a table for five.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: Tomasz might want to come too, he was asking.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Then six. Okay, I'll, um, I'll check. Right, I think that's it. I have to jump to another call.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: No. And I don't think we can sign for the bundled module knowing that it will no longer be supported after December and will have no security patches. So I think maybe we need to open the question again and look at what else is out there.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: So what are we looking at? The other one, the one with the capture feature?

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: The old one has no patches after December. The other one costs more but saves a lot of typing, and it has someone to call. So, the standalone accounts payable automation tool is what we're adopting. I'll tell Emeka today, and I'll ask Marisol to start on the contract.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: The module we picked, the bundled one, they stop supporting it at the end of this year. After December there are no security patches for it, none.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Is it really a problem? A year of use is a year of use. We could just replace it later.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: And the auditors. They'd ask about unpatched stuff straight away.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: So the thing is, it's got its own support team. If something breaks, it's their problem, not some ticket with the ERP people that sits for a month.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: And it pulls in our vendor list and account codes straight from the ERP, so no retyping that stuff, no master cleanup.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: The capture reads those. So nobody is keying them in. When I did the math on the typing time it comes to about sixty hours a month. Maybe a bit over.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Does it read badly scanned ones? Because we get some of those from the regional offices.

links.speaker: Ivan
links.quote: Who checks the reads? Like, when it gets an amount wrong?

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: And the approval limits would work the same?

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: They offered two. Um, the Tuesday and the Thursday after next. I think maybe Thursday is better because of the close.

links.speaker: Camila
links.quote: Thursday's fine with me. As long as it's the afternoon, I have the, the thing with the auditors in the morning.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: So Thursday afternoon then, for that. I'll confirm with them. Um, Camila, you sent me your questions, thank you.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: He, um, he looked at the number. He said the finance committee meets the week after the demo, so, we'll bring it there.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Not a formal one, no. But he didn't, he didn't seem against it.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Please don't change the number now.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: Sure. Okay.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Still waiting. I think maybe until Marisol is happy with the paper.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Plenty of time. Okay, can we do the expense memo? Because I found it.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Meals went up. It's sixty a day, not fifty-five.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Maybe someone could, um, put her files somewhere else in the meantime? Just so she's not sitting there.

links.speaker: Ivan
links.quote: I gave her a few reconciliations on a local copy. She's fine.

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: I told her to only use the one Stefan sent Monday.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: Good. Keep it that way.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Okay, okay. Um, I'll check the quote tonight and put it in the thread.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: If you have it, yes, send it to me. Thanks.

links.speaker: Ivan
links.quote: Me again. I don't mind.

links.speaker: Ravi
links.quote: You always say that. I can take half.

links.speaker: Ivan
links.quote: Honestly it's fine. I like the quiet.

links.speaker: Aisha
links.quote: Maybe next time, Pavel?

links.speaker: Pavel
links.quote: Next time. Yeah.
